newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/dollar futures sees only one trade.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/dollar futures sees only one trade.

text.p: South Africa's rand/dollar futures contracts made a sluggish debut on Wednesday as currency players took time to familiarise themselves with the workings of the new market, dealers said.
By 1125 GMT only one trade had taken place in the May contract, although bids and offers had been made for further dated instruments.
"Twenty contracts have been traded so far in one trade which is equivalent to about $2 million dollars," one trader said.
"It is a sluggish start. A lot of people are adopting a wait-and-see attitude at this stage. On the first day it is to be expected that the guys will be unsure," he said.

Dealing in the currency futures, which is seen as a further sign in the gradual relaxation of exchange controls, is limited to non-resident clients of members of the South African Futures Exchange (Safex) and authorised dealers.
Although Safex and the authorities aim to open the market over time as capital controls are dismantled, traders said that in the mean time market liquidity would be hampered.
"As people in the market have to have underlying foreign exchange regulation committment, there is no room for speculators. And you need speculators to get the liquidity going," one dealer said.
He said all eyes would be on the launch later on Wednesday of a competing dollar/rand product on the Chicago Mercentile Exchange.
"The one to look out for will be the CME this afternoon. They will have the 'gungho' speculators that we don't have."
A third contract was listed recently on FINEX, the financial products division of the New York Cotton Exchange, and trades in New York and Dublin.
Safex was not immediately available for comment.
